articles.title: Andy Taylor cause of death: The heartbreaking battle behind his final years
articles.standfirst: The Duran Duran guitarist continued making music and putting family first through a difficult final chapter
articles.summary: The Duran Duran guitarist continued making music and putting family first through a difficult final chapter
articles.body:
A ndy Taylor, the guitarist who helped shape Duran Duran’s sound, died at 65 after a battle with prostate cancer. His family and bandmates said he died peacefully at home on Nov. 23, surrounded by his family.

Simon Le Bon and his Duran Duran bandmates remembered Taylor as a force in the group from its early days, saying his playing helped drive the songs that took them around the world. Le Bon also shared how deeply he felt the loss, writing that there was a “massive Andy Taylor-shaped hole” in his heart.

Rod Stewart called Taylor his “dear pal.” The two worked together on Stewart’s 1988 album Out of Order , and Stewart recalled making music and having fun with him. Gary Kemp of Spandau Ballet also praised Taylor’s influence on the sound of the 1980s.

Other musicians shared tributes, including Chic co-founder Nile Rodgers, Belinda Carlisle and former Led Zeppelin frontman Robert Plant. Taylor played guitar on Carlisle’s “Mad About You” and appeared in its music video.

The guitarist who helped define Duran Duran’s sound

Taylor co-wrote songs including “Rio,” “Girls on Film” and “Save a Prayer.” His sharp, driving guitar lines became part of Duran Duran’s signature sound as the band rose to global fame in the 1980s. He also played with Robert Palmer in the short-lived group Power Station and released solo music.

His wife, Tracey, remembered him as “the rock of our family” and said family always came first. Taylor revealed in 2022 that he had been diagnosed with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer, explaining his absence from Duran Duran’s Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction . He later contributed to the band’s 2023 album Danse Macabre .
